reason: Control/role test fails: AuditFilter.filter only records an audit document (date, duration, Mongo insert) and its single decision is the audit.enabled property. There is no sanitizer, no session handling and no rate-limit key here; an mTLS/SPIFFE-header early return would merely skip the audit log (traceability loss), which is none of the claimed classes.

Target test fails: getRealIp already prefers X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For over the remote address, so the recipe is a no-op on the clean baseline; and on that baseline its only consumer is the audit log (RequestAudit), not a security decision. The genuine host for this class is the KeyResolver bean (injected as SCGD-002, where getRealIp is the tainted source).

Control/role and class-match tests fail: createAuditLog fills a DTO for logging and already takes the IP from the header-trusting IpUtils.getRealIp; replacing it with another header changes a log field, not a rate-limit key or any enforcement. The resulting defect would be log spoofing / traceability, not F115.
